title: Editing: Mull Of Kintyre by Wings | 1977
content:
Spirit of Ranachan Studio, Low Ranachan Farm, Campbeltown, Scotland
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Geoff Emerick, Mark Vigars

Following the recording of Wings’ ‘Mull Of Kintyre’, the song was edited on 10 August 1977.

Paul McCartney had concerns that the ending was not quite right, so he repeated an earlier section of the bagpipers and drummers playing the chorus. That resulted in the song’s length being reduced by 10 seconds.

‘Mull Of Kintyre’ still had guide vocals, and was completed on 3 October with the addition of new lead and harmony vocals, bass guitar, and acoustic guitar.

The day ended with a jam session, during which Wings recorded a piece known as ‘Jam (Day After Pipers)’. The following day they recorded another one titled ‘Jam (Good One)’, before a break in Wings recording sessions until October. The main reason for the break was the arrival of the McCartneys’ son James, who was born on 12 September.
